text:
Repair the supplied project according to CONTRACT.md. Deliver the complete deliverable.pyz, maintainable source and concise handoff. Work directly in this project without delegation.

Repair the UTC session-ledger report project. Deliver deliverable.pyz,
maintainable source and concise tested handoff. Python 3 standard library only.
Invocation: python deliverable.pyz INPUT_DIRECTORY --output RESULT_JSON
INPUT_DIRECTORY contains UTF-8 sessions.csv with named columns session,started_at,ended_at.
Column reordering, extra metadata, CSV quoting, CRLF/LF are legal. session is distinct,
exact nonempty text, including numeric-looking IDs, punctuation, whitespace or Unicode.
Each timestamp is YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS with optional 1-6 fractional digits followed by
Z or a numeric +/-HH:MM offset; it denotes an aware instant. Convert both instants to
UTC before ordering, subtraction or date grouping; never strip an offset as decoration.
For each input row emit {session:EXACT_TEXT,start_utc:CANONICAL,end_utc:CANONICAL,
seconds:NUMBER,start_utc_date:YYYY-MM-DD} in original input order. CANONICAL is exactly
YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ with six fractional digits. Group whole session durations
by their start UTC date (do not split midnight-spanning sessions), sorted by date.
Exit0 and JSON {sessions:[...],daily:[{date:DATE,sessions:INTEGER,seconds:NUMBER},...],
total_seconds:NUMBER}. Numeric tolerance is 1e-8 absolute. Zero durations are legal.
For the first row whose end instant precedes its start, exit2 and JSON
{error:{code:NEGATIVE_INTERVAL,session:EXACT_TEXT}} instead of a successful report.
Local clock labels can run backwards while elapsed UTC time is positive; equivalent
offset spellings represent the same instant. Preserve session text independently of
timestamp normalization. The final zipapp runs from arbitrary cwd with Python/inputs.
I’ll read the contract and current implementation, repair UTC handling, then test the rebuilt zipapp from outside the project directory.

The current parser truncates timestamps to 19 characters, losing both offsets and fractional seconds. I’ll convert endpoints to aware UTC datetimes and accumulate durations as integer microseconds. Tests will cover CSV variations, exact session text, UTC date grouping, and first-negative-row reporting through the packaged entry point.

The rebuilt zipapp passes the first five tests, including microsecond-negative intervals, backward local-clock labels with positive UTC durations, CSV variations, and exact session-text preservation. I’ll now test a copied standalone archive and check daily sorting across a year boundary.

Implemented and delivered **`deliverable.pyz`** in the project root, using only the Python standard library.

- **`main.py`**: maintainable source; preserves session text, converts endpoints to UTC before comparison and subtraction, emits six-digit fractional timestamps, and aggregates integer microseconds by start UTC date.
- **`build.py`**: rebuilds the standalone archive.
- **`test_ledger.py`**: packaged-entry-point regression tests.

**Verification:** `python -m unittest -v` — **7 tests passed**. Tests execute a copied archive from external temporary working directories and check CSV variations, exact IDs, offset equivalence, fractional precision, date boundaries, daily sorting, zero durations, and first-negative-interval exit status/error output. The supplied sample produces **120 total seconds**.

```bash
python deliverable.pyz INPUT_DIRECTORY --output RESULT_JSON
```

Rebuild and retest:
```bash
python build.py
python -m unittest -v
```

No commits were created; unrelated existing files were preserved.
